fp32_geometry_followup.definition: Resident HTTP request sent to first nonempty translated SSE text. Headers, readiness, prefill events, and empty token events do not count.
fp32_geometry_followup.adoption: Use four SIMD groups (128 threads) and two 8-row accumulators per group for every 64-token matrix tile. Preserve 32-token selection when it avoids additional padding. Remove the unused eight-group 64-token pipelines.

fp32_geometry_followup.candidate_vs_final: The measured candidate changes only the selector in the previous runtime. The final implementation additionally removes unused pipelines and renames the retained 64-token entry points. Final packaged measurements are recorded separately.

experiments.description: Real gate/up (4096 columns) and down (16384 columns) BF16 weights. Walk-order variants cover 69,116,225,443 uncached tokens. MPP covers 225,443. Per-variant median of five trials, three dispatches per trial, rotated order. All outputs compared bitwise; output buffers cleared before comparison.
experiments.walk_order: Row-first, token-first, grouped rows (2..64), and Morton blocks (2,4,8), over three tile geometries. No consistent long-input benefit from changing order.
experiments.mpp: Metal Performance Primitives matmul with relaxed_precision=false. Six tile shapes, BF16 and FP32 weights, dynamic and static extents. Bitwise agreement but slower than the existing long-input kernels; not adopted.

dense_arithmetic.assumptions: 32 layers; fixed 12-token prefix reused; final layer output projection/MLP for last row only; one output-head projection. Counts two operations per MAC. Excludes attention, norms, activation, I/O and launch overhead. This estimates work, not hardware peak throughput or a proven latency lower bound.

en-ja.limits: One persistent API worker, serialized single streams, 64 output tokens per request. Decode excludes startup/prefill. Wall rate uses SSE token arrivals. OS caching and other apps are uncontrolled.

runtime_observations.thermal_warning: No thermal/performance warnings recorded by pmset; this does not prove absence of throttling.
runtime_observations.interpretation: Memory pressure observed while the final en-ja process was active. At every completion, native explicit weight reads and fallback counters were zero. GPU prefill time increased, and some client-to-first-text delays also exceeded native timing. Correlation is not proof of the cause.

lossless_memory_followup.reason: Lossless packed weights used about 76% of the raw bytes in the measured gate/down tensors, but the same FP32 matrix kernel with packed loads was about 35–50% slower. Raw-buffer and texture variants were closer. This prototype does not establish that a full-model packed path would improve TTFT under memory pressure.
lossless_memory_followup.bitwise: PASS: all output elements, 69/116/225/443 uncached tokens, six variants each
lossless_memory_followup.limits: Microbenchmark uses two 64 MiB tensors, not the full model. A 6% system memory-free reading was observed during the preceding full-model API study; causal attribution remains unproven.

texture_extension.reason: Reading the existing packed layout from an RGBA32Uint texture was also bitwise exact, but slower than packed-buffer loads and approximately 2–3 times slower than the original BF16 texture kernel for long inputs.

precision_comparison.decision: Neither altered-precision 8B prototype meets one second for the measured 237/455-token API requests. Q4 also changes generated IDs in all four accuracy cases. Keep production FP32 unchanged.
precision_comparison.mixed_description: Texture BF16 weights retained, prefill matrix operands rounded to FP16 with weights scaled by 1024, FP32 accumulation; other operations unchanged.
precision_comparison.q4_description: 8B target weights quantized to existing symmetric group-32 Q4 format. New prefill matrix kernel dequantizes to scaled FP16 operands with FP32 accumulation. Comparison build explicitly reports q4-fp16 precision; not the production proposer.
precision_comparison.api_scope: One persistent API process per variant; prompt-token counts include the fixed translation template. First nonempty token.text event is timed from client send; one output token per request. Separate accuracy runs generate 64/64/16/16 tokens for 81/128/237/455-token inputs with speculation disabled.
precision_comparison.accuracy_limits: Four cases only. Same-prefix vector comparisons stop after the first divergent token. Token equality in the mixed comparison does not establish general quality equivalence or satisfy the FP32 arithmetic contract.

mlx.timing: host monotonic clock, synchronized GPU, one fresh operation per sample, seven rotated trials

microbenchmark.limits: MLX uses synchronized host wall time; native uses GPU command time. Different timings and numerical formats are not interchangeable. Matrix probes are not full API measurements. Corrected MPP baseline was rerun; invalid earlier run is excluded.

sustained_memory_followup.method: Normal speculation, speculation disabled, normal speculation. Separate persistent API process per mode, six alternating English/Japanese requests starting immediately after ready, 64 generated tokens each; no result caching. vm_stat and worker ps sampled before and after each request, outside timed HTTP request.
sustained_memory_followup.decision: No material TTFT benefit from disabling the proposer in this run. All 18 requests were below one second, but the earlier sustained slowdown was not reproduced. This is not a fix or evidence that the prior regression is resolved. Keep the default unchanged.
sustained_memory_followup.limits: Uncontrolled external workloads. vm_stat counters and wired memory are system-wide, not attribution to the worker. No OS memory or thermal settings were changed. Diagnostic subprocesses run between requests and can change idle timing.

coreml.precision: FP16 inputs and outputs; not the production FP32 contract

heterogeneous_comparison.coreml_conclusion: The gate tile is faster for long inputs, but the down tile is slower than the production Metal matrix probe. Core ML FP16 conv compute plans prefer the Neural Engine. FP32-typed ML programs exclude NE per the official documentation. No full 8B API implementation or TTFT claim.
heterogeneous_comparison.hybrid_method: Each matrix partitions output rows between the production Metal shader and concurrent Accelerate SGEMM. CPU shares are 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2. Test both preexpanded FP32 weights and BF16 expansion within the timed interval. Seven rotated trials. Recheck records host wall, GPU command duration, and CPU-side elapsed time separately.
heterogeneous_comparison.hybrid_conclusion: Initial isolated matrix comparisons were bitwise equal and some were faster. The subsequent complete 8B API prototype (api_prototype) regressed TTFT and is rejected. Production remains unchanged.
heterogeneous_comparison.limits: Isolated matrix tests, not an end-to-end 8B API benchmark. Core ML token lengths are padded shapes 96/128/256/448, whereas hybrid uses real 69/116/225/443 rows. Core ML output layout and conversion costs differ. GPU command and host times differ, external load and DVFS are uncontrolled. No production precision or inference path was changed. api_prototype contains separate full-model API/accuracy measurements; all other entries remain isolated matrix probes.

api_prototype.description: Comparison-only FP32 CPU/GPU prefill. GPU textures retain all original BF16 bits. Copy one quarter of each matrix to bounded shared scratch; restore exact BF16 bits and expand to FP32 for Accelerate. Shared-event callbacks overlap disjoint CPU/GPU output rows. Decode and short prefixes retain the original path. Extra scratch: 64 MiB raw + 128 MiB FP32.

cases.text: Translation quality depends on context, terminology, and the structure of the original document. api_prototype.decision: Do not adopt: CPU/GPU row partitioning is slower in complete HTTP/SSE measurements despite exact numerical outputs in the separate full-vector probe. Shared-event synchronization and texture copies are included in the measured path; their individual contributions were not separately profiled.

split_k_followup.decision: Reject the split-K candidate. Matrix-only timing improvements did not carry over to HTTP TTFT. Preserve the production FP32 worker.
split_k_followup.method: 24 matrix variants: N=32/64, K=8/16/32, 1/2/4/8 output partials. Original BF16 weights and FP32 operands/accumulation. Five rotated trials, three dispatches per trial including the reduction. Uncached input lengths 69,116,225,443. Partial sums change the addition order. Outputs cleared and compared against the original K16/N32 FP32 kernel; all finite and relative L2 below 1e-4.
split_k_followup.candidate: Use four FP32 output partials only for narrow 32-token panels with 65..96 uncached tokens; preallocate 64 MiB partial scratch. Other input lengths keep the original path.
split_k_followup.api_method: Original -> candidate -> original. Fresh API processes, no warmup requests, HTTP/SSE first nonempty token text. Original fixed 12-token translation prefix cache only. Seven requests per process; output limit one token. No claim about sustained decoding or full candidate generation accuracy.

Translation quality depends on context, terminology, and the structure of the original document. A useful system should preserve numbers, dates, and product names while producing natural sentences. This benchmark compares the same full precision model on the CPU and the GPU. It measures the delay before the first output token and the time spent generating subsequent tokens, while checking the translated text and the numerical differences between the two implementations.

arithmetic_probe.method: 4096 threadgroups of 128 threads; 1024 iterations; 4/8/16 independent accumulators. SIMD-group FP32 8x8x8 multiply-accumulate versus FP32 vector fma. Seven rotated trials; no large input matrices or attention. Original first probe with identical vector components discarded; scalar vector lanes now read independent seed values.
arithmetic_probe.excludes: Attention, norms, nonlinear activation, weight transfers, synchronization and HTTP. The final layer computes all QKV rows but only the last output/MLP row.
arithmetic_probe.interpretation: Measured SIMD-group arithmetic reaches about 3.1 TFLOP/s. The current 455-token computation requires 6.586 TFLOP before attention and other work, or over 6.586 TFLOP/s to fit in one second. This illustrates insufficient measured compute headroom on this machine; it is not a formal hardware peak or a proven lower bound for every possible algorithm.

limits: GPU clocks, thermal state and external workloads are uncontrolled.
Microbenchmark timings do not establish end-to-end speedups; the candidate failed that check.
The existing sustained short-request regression is still unresolved.
No precision, input limit, model or hardware requirement was relaxed.

API comparison caveat: the candidate did not auto-discover the 0.8B proposer (ready.speculative.enabled=false), while both original runs enabled it. Output limit one skips proposer prefill, but resident memory and process load still differ. The candidate showed no improvement even with less resident proposer memory; this is not a fully configuration-matched causal speed comparison.

strassen_followup.method: One-level Strassen factorization of X * W^T. Seven matrix products replace eight half-sized classical products. Original BF16 texture bits expanded exactly to FP32; weight and activation combinations, matrix operands, accumulators and final combination remain FP32. No FP16 or quantization. Changes addition order.
strassen_followup.shapes: Real 8B gate/up and down matrix tiles; uncached token counts 69,116,225,443. Token axis zero-padded to a multiple of 16. Seven Strassen tile variants plus two production baselines. Five rotated timing trials with three complete operations per trial, including all partial products and output combination.
strassen_followup.accuracy: Every output compared with the production FP32 kernel after clearing the output buffer. All finite and relative L2 below 1e-4. Matrix-only validation; no full-model token/quality equivalence claim.
strassen_followup.decision: Reject for long inputs: 116/225/443-token matrix execution regressed. At 69 uncached tokens, gate improved about 9% and down about 3% in the microbenchmark; this remains an unverified end-to-end candidate. Production unchanged.
strassen_followup.limits: One-level factorization and the listed tile shapes only. No claim that every fast matrix multiplication algorithm is impossible. GPU clocks, memory pressure and external load uncontrolled. Target remains unmet for long inputs.

short_input_candidate.method: Apply N40 Strassen only to complete direct texture rows at 65..80 uncached tokens; K8 for columns<8192 and K16 otherwise. GPU partial scratch 16 MiB. Same explicit original 0.8B proposer for every API process.
